Category response probabilities of the rating scale model

Source: R/fct_rsm.R
Pi_rsm.Rd

The probability of each answer category, and its first derivative, at an ability value, under the rating scale model of Andrich (1978): $$P(X = k \mid \theta) = \frac{\exp \sum_{t=1}^{k} D(\theta - (\lambda_j + \delta_t))} {\sum_{h=0}^{m} \exp \sum_{t=1}^{h} D(\theta - (\lambda_j + \delta_t))}$$ with the empty sum of category 0 equal to zero. It returns the same result as catR::Pi(model = "RSM").

Pi_rsm(theta, bank, D = 1)

Arguments

theta

Ability.

bank

Matrix of item parameters, one row per item: column 1 is the location of the item \(\lambda_j\), the other columns the thresholds \(\delta_1\) to \(\delta_m\), the same in every row (which makes it the rating scale and not the partial credit model). A 5-point Likert item, scored 0 to 4, needs 5 columns.

D

Metric constant, 1 or 1.702.

Value

A list: Pi, the probabilities, one row per item and one column per category, and dPi, their first derivatives.

See also

Other rating scale model: Ii_rsm(), density_function(), eap_est_rsm(), eap_se_rsm(), integrate_cat(), likelihood_rsm(), next_item_rsm()

Examples

bank <- matrix(c(-0.560, -0.230, 1.559, 0.071, 0.129,
                 rep(1.715, 5), rep(0.461, 5), rep(-1.265, 5), rep(-0.687, 5)),
               nrow = 5,
               dimnames = list(1:5, c("lambdaj", "delta1", "delta2", "delta3", "delta4")))
Pi_rsm(theta = 0, bank)$Pi
#>             cat0       cat1        cat2        cat3        cat4
#> Item1 0.08827106 0.02781046 0.030704594 0.190454305 0.662759579
#> Item2 0.23732018 0.05375358 0.042666335 0.190263548 0.475996359
#> Item3 0.95403130 0.03611457 0.004790796 0.003570467 0.001492864
#> Item4 0.45604320 0.07644622 0.044906724 0.148203679 0.274400176
#> Item5 0.50098691 0.07924783 0.043929232 0.136808204 0.239027827
rowSums(Pi_rsm(theta = 0, bank)$Pi) # each item's probabilities add up to 1
#> Item1 Item2 Item3 Item4 Item5 
#>     1     1     1     1     1
